newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan open for meeting with China at APEC - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan open for meeting with China at APEC - paper.

text.p: Taiwan has not ruled out the possibility of a meeting between its top China negotiator and the mainland leadership at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, the United Evening News said on Tuesday.

It said Koo Chen-fu, chairman of the semi-official Straits Exchange Foundation, will be Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui's representative at the APEC summit in the Philippines later this month, opening the door to a rare encounter with the Chinese president after 17 months of sometimes tense hostilities.
Koo could separately meet with Chinese President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin who will also be attending the November 25-26 Subic Bay summit, the newspaper said.
But such a meeting would depend on China's attitude, the newspaper quoted Chang King-yuh, chairman of the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, as saying.
The council is Taiwan's top policymaking body toward China.
The Philippines has rejected Taiwan's request that Lee or Vice-President Lien Chan be allowed to attend the summit.
Koo represented the Taiwanese president at last year's APEC summit in Osaka, Japan, but exchanged nothing more than a tense handshake with Jiang.

China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and strives to isolate Lee and his exiled Chinese Nationalist government. Taiwan sits in APEC as a customs territory, not a sovereign state.
Taipei officially espouses reunification but does not accept terms offered by Beijing, insisting that China first adopt democratic reforms like those carried out in Taiwan.
